the manipulation of rumen microbiota and rumen metabolism by using prophylactics and prebiotics is a promising strategy for the mitigation of methane production from ruminants.

the prophylactic options to mitigate rumen methane emission have been developed in Japan, and the prophylactic effect of nisin on methane emission from raminants has been demonstrated in the in vitro and in situ trials.
the prophylactic options for mitigation of methane emission from animal agriculture are the administration of L-cystine, nisin, saponin, cashew nutshell liquid, and PRA to ruminants.

the mitigation of rumen methane emission by the manipulation of rumen microbes with the aim of developing new feed additives and feed supplements.
the development of prophylactic manipulators to mitigate rumen methane emissions and to secure safety for ruminants and their products and environment in Japan.
the development of prophylactics to mitigate methane emission from rumanit livestock, and the development of a new inventory of mitigation technologies to target ruminants in Asian and Pacific areas.
